![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066197/assets/acdc98dc5a658e7c945dca00c1a1c0a73d87e3dc98db8071a534a4fd7f215c90.png)

decisions.question: e-4840

source.question: e-4840
source.value:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,\mathbf{x}\,]_{\mathcal{B}} = P_{\small\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{B}} [\,\mathbf{x}\,]_{\mathcal{C}} .
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix $P_{\small\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{B}}$ from $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{B}.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of $P_{\small\mathcal{B}\to\mathcal{C}}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 6 & -4\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-4)(-4)-6\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}-4 & -3 \\ -6 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & \frac{3}{2} \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $\mathbf{x} = 2 \mathbf{c}_1-6\mathbf{c}_2,$ we obtain
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066197/assets/883431c76485c9fd706fe79c2bf3936946cfb0dba602ebd0df77d6cc9e800665.png)

Now, we compute $[\,\mathbf{x}\,]_{\mathcal{B}}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & \frac{3}{2} \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066197/assets/0dcc93449ac1d14e51850e4a74f639aeb3acd21b720ba2b9deeb2208d9fffeb4.png)

decisions.question: e-4841

source.question: e-4841
source.value:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,\mathbf{x}\,]_{\mathcal{B}} = P_{\small\mathcal{S}\to\mathcal{B}} [\,\mathbf{x}\,]_{\mathcal{S}} .
$$

First, recall that the change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{S}$ is the matrix whose columns are the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ relative to the standard basis $\mathcal{S}.$ As a result, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066197/assets/50bbd2dd0fa1c0732a01d07c2614ab15549272fcc0b7d686651f0464b3b50f39.png)

Now, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix $P_{\small\mathcal{S}\to\mathcal{B}}$ from $\mathcal{S}$ to $\mathcal{B}.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of $P_{\small\mathcal{B}\to\mathcal{S}}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S\to B} & ={P}_{B\to S}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 10\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 10-3\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}10 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we compute $[\,\mathbf{x}\,]_{\mathcal{B}}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{S\to B}[\,x\,]_{S} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

source.question: e-7276
source.value:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ as $\{ \mathbf{b}_1,\mathbf{b}_2 \}$ and $\{ \mathbf{c}_1,\mathbf{c}_2 \},$ respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{C}$ is a matrix whose columns are the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}.$

So, we need to find the coordinates of $\mathbf{b}_1$ and $\mathbf{b}_2$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066197/assets/034a2a4079120d719f9061c339899f9aed9b50a765200291ca15c500ef647a70.png)

Reducing the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 6 & 13 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 11 & 15 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the change-of-coordinates matrix $P_{\small\mathcal{B}\to\mathcal{C}}$ is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066197/assets/8d07812ea170bcbb56264468f4cfd0fa8b88cf4f68f9b50d35f61e9e33de45c3.png)

Finally, we compute $[\,\mathbf{x}\,]_{\mathcal{C}}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 & 15 \\ -5 & -7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
